message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time or predictive air‑quality data. For up‑to‑date information on the Air Quality Index (AQI) in New York—or any other location—you could try one of the following:

| Resource | What it offers |
|----------|----------------|
| **EPA’s AirNow** – https://www.airnow.gov/ | Current AQI readings, historical trends, and short‑term forecasts from U.S. EPA monitoring stations. |
| **AirVisual / IQAir** – https://iqair.com/, https://www.iqair.com/us/new-york-city-new-york | Real‑time AQI maps, daily summaries, and some forecasting based on satellite & ground sensors. |
| **OpenWeatherMap “Air Pollution” API** – https://openweathermap.org/api/air-pollution | Provides hourly/daily PM2.5, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂ levels along with calculated AQI if requested. |
| **Local NYC Environmental Agencies** – e.g., NY State Department of Environmental Conservation | City‑wide reports, long‑range planning documents, and links to official monitoring networks. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot right now, visiting *AirNow* or using the *OpenWeatherMap Air Pollution API* would likely give you the most reliable numbers. If you’d prefer automated updates, many of those services also allow you to set alerts when AQI crosses certain thresholds.
